## Referenced Standards

- IEEE 29148-2018 — uniquely identified and traceable requirements
- IEEE 1016-2009 — design-description identifiers
- ISO/IEC 42001 — AI governance controls and evidence
- `docs/architecture/DOC-ARCHITECTURE-ZURI-HYBRID.md`

## 1. Scope / ขอบเขต

This scheme applies to **new standalone requirements created after adoption**. It supplements the
existing Zuri namespaces; it does not replace or renumber them.

Existing `CR-*`, `FEAT-*`, `ADR-*`, `ZDEV-*`, `TSK-ZUMP01*`, `AC1`, and `NFR1` identifiers remain
valid in their original documents. When an old requirement needs cross-document traceability,
record it as an alias rather than rewriting history.

## 2. Prefix Registry

| Prefix | Category | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `FR-xxx` | Functional Requirements | `FR-001` Tenant-scoped customer search |
| `NFR-xxx` | Non-Functional Requirements | `NFR-001` P95 API latency target |
| `SDD-xxx` | Software Design Decisions | `SDD-001` Outbound-only data transport |
| `SEC-xxx` | Security Requirements | `SEC-001` Fail-closed login rate limit |
| `AI-AGT-xxx` | AI Agent Specifications | `AI-AGT-001` Reply-confidence gate |
| `AI-ETH-xxx` | AI Ethics & Governance | `AI-ETH-001` Human approval for price changes |
| `BR-xxx` | Business Rules | `BR-001` No marketing without consent |
| `AC-xxx` | Acceptance Criteria | `AC-001` Non-consented recipient is skipped |
| `DR-xxx` | Data Requirements | `DR-001` Export payload excludes direct PII |
| `IR-xxx` | Infrastructure Requirements | `IR-001` Redis PONG before deploy trust |

`xxx` is a zero-padded, repository-wide sequence within the prefix. IDs are never reused.

## 3. Allocation Procedure

1. Read `docs/.requirement-id-counters.json` immediately before allocation.
2. Select the `next` value for the required prefix.
3. Add the requirement and update `last_issued` plus `next` in the same change.
4. Search `docs/` and `gks/` for the proposed ID before finalizing.
5. If concurrent work already consumed the number, allocate a new number; do not force-renumber
   the other approved change.
6. Link the requirement to its owner document, acceptance evidence, and supersession state.

The counter file is coordination metadata, not proof that a requirement exists. The canonical
requirement text remains in its governed document.

## 4. Required Fields

Every new standalone requirement records:

| Field | Required content |
|---|---|
| ID | Allocated identifier |
| Title | Short behavior or constraint |
| Statement | Testable SHALL/SHALL NOT language |
| Rationale | Why the requirement exists |
| Source | CR, product goal, incident, law, or approved decision |
| Owner | Named role or person |
| Status | `draft`, `approved`, `implemented`, `verified`, `retired`, or `superseded` |
| Acceptance evidence | Test, runtime check, artifact, approval, or explicit `pending` |
| Links | Upstream and downstream traceability references |

`implemented` and `verified` are distinct states. Code existence alone does not satisfy
verification.

## 5. Compatibility Rules

- Do not bulk-convert `AC1` to `AC-001` or `NFR1` to `NFR-001`.
- Do not allocate ADR numbers here; use `gks/00_index/atomic_index.jsonl` and the MSP workflow.
- Do not allocate CR or FEAT numbers here; their existing program and blueprint registries remain
  authoritative.
- A requirement may cite a legacy ID using `aliases`, for example `aliases: ["CR-003:AC1"]`.
- A superseded ID stays searchable and points to its replacement; it is never recycled.

## 6. Validation

Initial validation is manual and read-only:

- JSON parsing of the counter registry
- repository-wide collision search
- path existence for linked local artifacts
- evidence/state review before claiming `verified`

Automated drift and collision guards belong to DOC-RECON-06 and require their own approved
failure/success fixtures before implementation.
